content:
Similar to what you've tried, this is how I've always done it (Windows). It preserves your whole existing setup.

1. Copy TB files from the old PC

- launch TB on the old PC

- go to TB menu > Help > Troubleshooting Information

- click the Application Basics > Profile Folder 'Open Folder' button

- the profile folder will open

- navigate three levels up to the AppData\Roaming folder

- close TB

- copy the AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird folder to a flash drive

2. Install and launch TB on the new PC, then start setting up the new profile. Skip to the next section if you've already installed TB and created a profile.

- on the 'Set Up Your Existing Email Address' screen, enter name and email address only

- click the 'Configure manually' link

- scroll down and click 'Cancel'

- exit setup

- close TB

3. Paste the copied TB files to the new PC

- open the AppData\Roaming folder like you did above

- delete the Thunderbird folder, or copy it somewhere if you want to save it

- replace it with the Thunderbird folder from the flash drive

- launch TB

content:
Have you thought of doing it directly server to server via webmail? https://support.microsoft.com/en-gb/office/turn-on-automatic-forwarding-in-outlook-7f2670a1-7fff-4475-8a3c-5822d63b0c8e#picktab=web

Then your gmail imap account would synch with server and download everything.

In Thunderbird When you right click on highlighted emails and use 'Copy-to' gmail Inbox, that is uploading to gmail server via imap.

Gmail have limits on uploading via imap. https://support.google.com/a/answer/1071518?hl=en

If you have an Anti-Virus scanning everything then it can take forever as it scans everything being downloaded/uploaded and also every file that gets opened. Sometimes things seem to drop out. Hence advise on using 'Copy -to' and not 'Move-to' as that second option may delete emails off the original server - if something goes wrong and you use 'Copy-to' at least you can repeate the action. Suggestion - Access Anti-Virus and set up an exclusion to not scan anything in your Thunderbird profile folder.

The folder pane shows your folders such as "Inbox" and "Deleted". Just right click on the "Deleted" folder to get the option to empty the trash. Some e-mail accounts put trash in a "Deleted" or "Deleted Items" folder. Others put it in a "Trash" folder. All the same.

content:
First you say you want to get outlook mail account emails put into the gmail account: Would like to push EVERYTHING downloaded to Outlook folders (from Outlook.live.com) to my GMail account folders.

But then you say the opposite: Attempting to let TB move the Gmail files to the Outlook folders.

If you want to get copies of emails you have in the outlook imap mail account put into the gmail imap account.

Please note: Never use 'move' because the outlook server sees 'move' as a move off server - basically a deletion. You do not want to do any deleting until you know the email has been successfully copied into the gmail account.

In Thunderbird. In imap outlook account: Select a batch of emails to highlight them.

  • left click on first email, press down 'shift' key and click on last email of batch - all in between are highlighted.
  • right click on the highlighted emails and select 'Copy to' and choose the appropriate imap gmail folder.

Repeat this 'Copy to' a gmail folder until all outlook emails are copied over to gmail.

In imap gmail account - do check you can open and read those emails - if you have only copied headers then you will not see email content. You may need to ensure you are downloading full copies.

Once you have got full copies in gmail account then you can delete them off the outlook imap account if required.

Once you are up to date and it's only new mail coming in to outlook imap account, then you can create a Message Filter to do it automatically.

  • Tools > Message Filter
  • Click on 'New'
  • Give suitable name like 'Outlook to Gmail'
  • Select 'Getting new mail'
  • select 'Filter after Junk classification' - if you do not want to get copies of anything in Spam folder.
  • select 'Match all messages'
  • Perform these actions
  • 'Copy Message to' and choose 'gmail account Inbox'
  • Click on 'Save'
  • Make sure filter is enabled.

Suggest you do this as well:

  • click on 'Filter Log'
  • Select the 'Enable the filter log' checkbox.
  • click on 'Close'

Then you can close the Message Filter window. All new emails that arrive in the outlook imap Inbox will then get auto copied to the gmail imap Inbox.

re :This morning the Customized Menu Bar in my T-Bird was there, as confirmed by my wife... and then it wasn't.

We need to clarify what you are talking about.

What OS do you use? I'm assuming Windows, but it's something you should let us know about. What version of Thunderbird ar you using ? Important to know because layout and instructions vary depending upon version.

The 'Menu Bar' toolbar cannot be customised. The 'Menu Bar' toolbar is the one with 'File, Edit, View, Go, Message, Events & Tasks, Tools, Help'. It's a really useful toolbar. You can initialise it via the 'Menu app icon' - it has 3 horizontal lines. 'Menu app icon' > 'View' > 'Toolbars > select 'Menu Bar'


There is a new 'Unified Toolbar' which can be customised and it works similar to the old 'Mail Toolbar', however thenew Unified toolbar is now used in various tabs and can be customised depending upon the tab you are using. So if you set it up for the 'Mail' tab and then were viewing th Calendar or Address Book, then the Unified toolbar will look different.

Info on 'Unified Toolbar': https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/unified-toolbar
